description: PAR sheet (Probability and Accounting Report). The formal mathematics document for a slot game and the core artefact reviewed by test laboratories and regulators. See steering/math-verification.md section 3.
instructions: Section 14 (wager configuration matrix) is the most commonly omitted section and the one most likely to fail certification. GLI-11 and GLI-19 both require the minimum RTP to hold across ALL wager configurations.
Section 8 RTP must match the in-game disclosure exactly.
Bind this document to a specific build hash (section 1). Certification applies to a build, not to a product.

section1_gameIdentification.notes: GLI-11 requires a message digest of at least 128 bits where hashing is used for program identification.

section4_reelStrips.notes: Where virtual weighted mapping is used, list BOTH physical and virtual strips. Probability must be computed from the virtual positions; computing from physical symbols yields an incorrect distribution.

section6_paylineDefinitions.notes: Provide coordinates for each line so probabilities can be independently recomputed.

section7_rules.notes: Evaluation order must be explicit. The implementation and the theoretical calculation must use the same order.

section8_rtpBreakdown.notes: Compute with rational or high-precision arithmetic. 32-bit float accumulation over tens of millions of terms can shift the third decimal place, which is enough to break agreement with the laboratory's recomputation.

section9_hitFrequency.notes: effectiveHitFrequency is the proportion of spins returning MORE than the stake. It is required because UK RTS 14F and Ontario Standard 2.20 prohibit celebrating returns at or below the stake. A product driving audio-visual feedback from total hit frequency will breach those rules.

section10_volatility.notes: probabilityOfMaximumPrize is MANDATORY for Germany (GlueStV section 22a(3) requires disclosing it) and is needed for Brazil (the advertised top prize must be winnable at least once per 100 million plays).

section11_simulationResults.notes: Sample size must be derived from target precision and measured sigma, not from convention. GLI-11 and GLI-19 impose no fixed sample size for software RNGs; the requirement is that the data volume can detect significant deviations with high frequency. Extremely low-frequency high-value prizes should be handled analytically rather than by brute-force simulation - state that treatment in longTailHandling.

section12_featureDetails.notes: For retriggers, expected total spins converges as n / (1 - p*k). If p*k is at or above 1 the model diverges, which is itself a design error.

section13_jackpotDetails.notes: Germany PROHIBITS jackpots (GlueStV section 22a(8) Jackpotverbot). A German build requires a separate maths model with the jackpot contribution redistributed, not a disabled flag. See GLI-12 for progressive jackpot requirements.

section14_wagerConfigurationMatrix.notes: MANDATORY AND FREQUENTLY OMITTED. GLI-11 and GLI-19 require the minimum RTP to hold for all wager configurations. Pennsylvania measures the 85% floor at the LOWEST single-play wager and the sub-100% ceiling at the HIGHEST eligible wager. Michigan requires RTP at both highest and lowest skill levels where skill affects RTP. GLI-19 section 4.7.1 requires skill-affected games to meet the floor under optimal play. Designs where RTP rises with stake commonly fail at the minimum bet.

disclosureConsistency.notes: UK RTS 3C requires RTP or chance of winning to be disclosed before the player commits, and RTS 9 requires jackpot RTP disclosure. Germany section 22a(3) requires the average payout per EUR 1 stake AND the maximum-prize probability at the point the stake is placed. Ontario Standard 4.07 requires disclosure of restrictions including maximum wins.
